maya: Heads-up — bringing up monarch16b-int4 on canary. Initial smoke looks ok but hitting OOMs when requests do `max_new_tokens > 256` :grimacing:
raj: thanks. can you paste the exact error/log? rough guess: kv cache growth + fragmentation on int4 image
elin: monarch has a deeper kv layout than other 16B models we onboarded. int4 increases activation churn. we should try lowering `max_new_tokens` default and test slot compactor thresholds
sasha: log snippet from one pod:
```
E202-03-12 09:12:11.342 | oom: allocation failed: cudaMalloc(size=2147483648)
W202-03-12 09:12:11.343 | kv_cache_size=1.8G, resident=2.1G, fragmentation=23%
I202-03-12 09:12:11.344 | request: user gen len=320, batch_size=2, max_new_tokens=512
```
raj: that fragmentation number is telling. try `--slot-compactor=aggressive` on a canary and reduce microbatch to 1 for a test run
maya: ran quick canary with compactor and set max_new_tokens=128 — no OOMs. perf hit on long generations tho (latency up ~18%)
elin: expected. two ideas: 1) enable prefix-KV caching for conversational flows to reduce per-token ops, 2) set a conservative default `max_new_tokens=128` on hosted for monarch16b-int4 and document it
tomas: also try disabling prefetch for int4 path — we've seen prefetch + int4 cause transient memory spikes (prefetch reserves contiguous buffers)
maya: did an A/B: prefetch off vs on. with prefetch ON we had 2x OOM rate. OFF -> stable but CPU latency rose slightly. results in /tmp/monarch_ab.csv (small table)
sasha: on the quality side — int4 gives a tiny drop in generation coherence on our summarization eval (instr-follow F1 down 1.6 pts). we tried per-channel scaling (symmetric) and that recovered ~0.8 pts
raj: is cost win worth quality delta? what's tokens/sec delta vs nebula20b baseline?
elin: bench summary:
- monarch16b-int4 (prefetch OFF, max_new_tokens=128): 620 tok/s, 0.8% regression vs float16 quality
- nebula20b-quant (our current 16B baseline): 410 tok/s, baseline quality
so monarch int4 is faster but has a measurable quality hit unless we apply per-channel scale calibration
maya: proposed short-term plan: set hosted default max_new_tokens=128 for monarch16b-int4, disable prefetch for int4 kernels, enable slot compactor aggressive, and run a 24h canary with eval hooks. if quality still below threshold -> try tiny int8 per-layer mix for attention weights
tomas: for OOM mitigation patch, I can push a runtime safegate to force microbatch=1 on large gens when fragmentation >15% until compaction happens
infra-bot: deploy queued for `monarch-int4-canary` image v1.3.2 — canary target 3 pods
deploy-bot: canary started at 09:18 — monitoring logs at https://grafana.internal/redwood/monarch-canary
maya: i'll kick off canary and attach eval job. assigning action items:
- maya: run 24h canary + eval (instr-follow, summarization)
- sasha: run per-channel scale calibration sweep and upload weights
- tomas: runtime safegate PR
- raj: update docs + release notes for default max_new_tokens change
maya: will post results in this thread tomorrow. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
